title: Provenance Loss and Repair in Multilingual Compaction
abstract: arXiv:2611.31668v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Conversational assistants compact older messages into short notes and evict the originals. When the note's language requires a distinction that English leaves open, such as Spanish adjective gender (agotado vs. agotada), messages that omit or explicitly state that attribute can yield the same note. After eviction, later turns cannot tell them apart: taking the inflected form literally asserts an attribute the user never gave, whereas discounting it as routine grammar discards one the user did give. We propose a training-free repair across writing, pre-eviction verification and reading. The writer marks unstated attributes with paired forms (e.g., agotado/a), a likelihood check before eviction rewrites unsupported single forms into paired ones, and the reader trusts remaining single forms as stated facts. On five Qwen3.5 and Gemma-4 models, eviction cuts recall of stated attributes from 90% to 34% in question answering (QA); our repair

translated_title: 多语言压缩中的来源信息丢失与修复
translated_abstract: arXiv:2611.31668v1 公告类型： cross 摘要：会话型助手会将较早的对话消息压缩成简短笔记并丢弃原始消息。当笔记所用的语言需要作出英语中不作区分的区分时，例如西班牙语形容词的性属变化（agotado vs. agotada），省略该属性或明确声明该属性的消息可能产生相同的笔记。在原始消息被丢弃后，后续对话无法再区分这两种情况：将词形变化按字面理解会断言一个用户从未提供过的属性，而将其视为常规语法而忽略则会丢弃用户确实提供过的属性。我们提出了一种无需训练的修复方法，涵盖写作、丢弃前验证和阅读三个环节：写入者用成对形式（如 agotado/a）标注未声明的属性，丢弃前的似然检查将缺乏依据的单式形式改写为成对形式，而阅读者则将剩余的单式形式视为已声明的事实。在五个 Qwen3.5 和 Gemma-4 模型上，消息丢弃使问答（QA）中对已声明属性的召回率从 90% 降至 34%；我们的修复方法……
tldr: 该论文发现多语言对话压缩会因语法性别等语言差异而丢失属性的来源信息（无法区分用户明确声明与语法默认），并提出一种无需训练、覆盖写作标注、丢弃前似然验证和阅读信任三个环节的修复方法，大幅恢复被压缩丢弃的已声明属性召回率。
en_tdlr: This paper identifies provenance loss in multilingual conversational compaction—where gendered languages cannot distinguish user-stated attributes from grammatical defaults—and proposes a training-free repair spanning paired-form annotation at write time, pre-eviction likelihood verification, and reader-side trust, substantially restoring recall of stated attributes.
